paper.title: Public Versus Private Providers: How Ownership Impacts Quality in Public Service Markets
paper.code_data_availability: Data Availability Statement (p. 320): "The full data set for this study cannot be made available online due to privacy or ethical restrictions stemming from the applied survey data and register data on ownership. …

registers.name_in_paper: Statistics Denmark (national agency charged with the official registration of center ownership)
Nationwide survey of childcare center directors (distributed through SurveyMonkey)
variables_mentioned: percent enrolled children with two or more languages
additional resources for children with special needs

registers.name_in_paper: De Kommunale Noegletal / administrative data from the Ministry of the Interior and Health
registers.role: local-government-level controls; user fee for public and nonprofit centers
variables_mentioned: children of sole providers per 100 0-17-year-old children
monthly rate for childcare centers for 3-5-year-old children

registers.name_in_paper: Manually collected user-fee data from for-profit providers' websites or direct contact
variables_mentioned: monthly user fee paid by parents

linkages: Childcare centers linked to their registered ownership form through the Statistics Denmark population list of all 3468 Danish childcare centers for 3-5- and 0-5-year-olds
Childcare centers linked to their local government (municipality) so that municipal administrative indicators from De Kommunale Noegletal can be attached
Survey responses linked to the center's registered ownership and to the manually collected user fee

sample.universe: The full population of 3468 Danish childcare centers for 3-5- and 0-5-year-olds in 2018 supplied by Statistics Denmark; in 2018 this corresponded to 2480 public, 501 for-profit and 487 nonprofit providers.
selection_rules: Start from the Statistics Denmark list of the full population of 3468 childcare centers for 3-5- and 0-5-year-olds, containing name, ownership and contact information
Disproportional stratified random sample: 1000 randomly selected public centers plus all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers
Survey distributed to a slightly smaller number of centers because of errors in the population list (e.g. permanently closed institutions): 979 public, 489 for-profit and 475 nonprofit, total 1943

591 centers completed or partially completed the survey (477 completed, 114 partially completed), a response rate of approx. 30%; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers
Only centers under the Danish law on childcare provision are included, excluding a small fraction of Danish centers established under the law on public schools
In age-integrated centers the respondent was asked to answer only for the 3-5-year-old (kindergarten) children
Estimation samples range from N = 178 to N = 390 depending on item non-response for the particular indicator
sample.n_observations: N in the reported models ranges from 178 to 390 childcare centers (most models N = 390)
sample.n_individuals: 591 responding childcare centers (249 public, 134 nonprofit, 208 for-profit)

construction_notes: The staff-child ratio is calculated rather than the more commonly used child-staff ratio, because Stata treats observations as missing when the denominator is 0 (e.g. centers reporting no full-time teachers employed)
Numbers of newly hired and departing pedagogical employees in the last 12 months were transformed into variables measuring turnover as a percent of the entire staff
Parent-center collaboration is measured by three index variables built from five, three and four survey items respectively, each measured from 1 (low degree) to 5 (high degree)

Quality is conceptualized with Donabedian's framework: five structural categories (staff-child ratio, staff qualifications, staff continuity, group size, physical surroundings) and four process categories (parent-staff collaboration, outdoor practices, caregiver-child interaction, specialized services), 27 indicators in total
Ownership enters as two dummies (for-profit, nonprofit) with public as reference, plus a third dummy comparing nonprofit (=1) with for-profit (=0)
The number of childcare centers per local government was excluded from the final models because of multicollinearity with the number of 0-5-year-olds in the local government

Estimator matched to the dependent variable: logit for dummies, fractional regression for ratios and shares, OLS otherwise; average marginal effects reported for logit and fractional models, unstandardized coefficients for OLS
All reported significance levels are sharpened False Discovery Rate q-values (Simes method, corresponding to Benjamini-Hochberg) computed with the qvalue package in Stata 18
Robust standard errors clustered at the local government level in all models

For public and nonprofit centers the monthly user fee is the local government rate from the Ministry of the Interior and Health; for for-profit centers it was collected from their websites or by phone/email

claims.statement: Compared with public childcare centers, for-profit centers show no statistically significant difference in Full-time caregivers/Enrolled children, conditional on 11 center- and local-government-level controls.

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark: official registration of childcare center ownership (no register code or variable name given)

definition.value: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the childcare center is registered as a for-profit provider and 0 if it is a public provider; public ownership is the reference category. Ownership is taken from register data obtained from Statistics Denmark, the national agency charged with the official registration of center ownership.

timing.value: Ownership form as registered in the 2018 Statistics Denmark population list of childcare centers, i.e. measured at the time of the survey (cross-section, 2018).

definition.value: Number of full-time caregivers reported by the center divided by the number of enrolled children; caregivers are all staff whose primary function is the daily care of enrolled children (preschool teachers, childcare workers and teacher assistants). Both numbers are reported separately by the surveyed center director. The staff-child ratio (rather than the child-staff ratio) is used because Stata treats observations with a zero denominator as missing.

timing.value: The state of the center at the time of the 2018 survey, as reported by the center director. The study is a single 2018 cross-section, so the outcome is measured contemporaneously with the ownership form, not after it.

estimand.target_population: Center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds in Denmark that are under the Danish law on childcare provision; the contrast is for-profit versus public providers.
estimand.formal_query: E[Full-time caregivers/Enrolled children | ownership = for-profit, X] - E[Full-time caregivers/Enrolled children | ownership = public, X], with X the 11 center- and local-government-level controls (no do-operator: the authors state the design does not support causal inference).

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

key_assumptions.assumption: Center directors report the quality indicator without ownership-related reporting bias, so that differences between ownership forms are differences in the service and not in self-presentation.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author raises the threat explicitly and reports three mitigations: cognitive pretesting of items with directors of public, nonprofit and for-profit centers; an invitation email emphasising the research purpose and the aggregated, anonymous treatment of responses; and neutral, factual question wording.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimates are conditioned on survey response, and response propensity differs by ownership: the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from that of the distributed sample for public and for-profit centers.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Chi2 tests of the share of responses by ownership against the ownership distribution in the sample, reported in Table A1 in the Appendix; the author calls for caution in generalizing the results.

key_assumptions.assumption: Differences in financial resources across ownership, in particular the higher user fee that for-profit centers may charge at their own discretion, are captured by the monthly user-fee control, so remaining differences are not driven by resources.
key_assumptions.supported_by: User fees for all centers were collected (administrative data for public and nonprofit centers, websites or direct contact for for-profit centers) and the monthly rate is included as a control in every model.

threats_discussed: Cross-sectional design prevents causal inference and examination of developments over time
Possible selection in the geographical location of childcare providers and in parents' choice of a provider with a specific ownership form
Center directors may have an interest in responding more positively or negatively depending on ownership
Higher user fees and therefore more economic resources in private institutions could cause quality differences
The ownership distribution of survey responses differs significantly from that of the sample for public and for-profit centers, calling for caution in generalizing
Multiple hypothesis testing across a large number of dependent variables and models
Multicollinearity between the number of childcare centers per local government and the number of 0-5-year-olds, leading to exclusion of the former
Quality that is less readily observable cannot be assessed with survey and administrative data; this would require observational studies
robustness_checks: All reported significance levels adjusted for multiple hypothesis testing using sharpened False Discovery Rate q-values (Simes method / Benjamini-Hochberg) in Stata 18
Robust standard errors clustered at the local government level in all models
Monthly user fee included as a control, collected manually from websites or by direct contact for for-profit centers
Chi2 test of the ownership distribution in the sample versus in the responses (Table A1)
Full models with all control coefficients reported in Tables A2.1, A2.2, A3.1 and A3.2
Estimator chosen to match the nature of the dependent variable (logit, fractional or OLS), with average marginal effects reported for logit and fractional models
unresolved_confounders: The authors state the cross-sectional design and data do not facilitate causal inference regarding the effect of ownership on service quality
Selection of parents into providers with a specific ownership form, and of providers into geographical areas, is addressed only by observed local-government-level controls
Differential survey response by ownership (public and for-profit) is acknowledged but not corrected
Less readily observable dimensions of childcare quality are not measured

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

key_assumptions.assumption: Center directors report the quality indicator without ownership-related reporting bias, so that differences between ownership forms are differences in the service and not in self-presentation.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author raises the threat explicitly and reports three mitigations: cognitive pretesting of items with directors of public, nonprofit and for-profit centers; an invitation email emphasising the research purpose and the aggregated, anonymous treatment of responses; and neutral, factual question wording.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimates are conditioned on survey response, and response propensity differs by ownership: the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from that of the distributed sample for public and for-profit centers.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Chi2 tests of the share of responses by ownership against the ownership distribution in the sample, reported in Table A1 in the Appendix; the author calls for caution in generalizing the results.

key_assumptions.assumption: Differences in financial resources across ownership, in particular the higher user fee that for-profit centers may charge at their own discretion, are captured by the monthly user-fee control, so remaining differences are not driven by resources.
key_assumptions.supported_by: User fees for all centers were collected (administrative data for public and nonprofit centers, websites or direct contact for for-profit centers) and the monthly rate is included as a control in every model.

threats_discussed: Cross-sectional design prevents causal inference and examination of developments over time
Possible selection in the geographical location of childcare providers and in parents' choice of a provider with a specific ownership form
Center directors may have an interest in responding more positively or negatively depending on ownership
Higher user fees and therefore more economic resources in private institutions could cause quality differences
The ownership distribution of survey responses differs significantly from that of the sample for public and for-profit centers, calling for caution in generalizing
Multiple hypothesis testing across a large number of dependent variables and models
Multicollinearity between the number of childcare centers per local government and the number of 0-5-year-olds, leading to exclusion of the former
Quality that is less readily observable cannot be assessed with survey and administrative data; this would require observational studies
robustness_checks: All reported significance levels adjusted for multiple hypothesis testing using sharpened False Discovery Rate q-values (Simes method / Benjamini-Hochberg) in Stata 18
Robust standard errors clustered at the local government level in all models
Monthly user fee included as a control, collected manually from websites or by direct contact for for-profit centers
Chi2 test of the ownership distribution in the sample versus in the responses (Table A1)
Full models with all control coefficients reported in Tables A2.1, A2.2, A3.1 and A3.2
Estimator chosen to match the nature of the dependent variable (logit, fractional or OLS), with average marginal effects reported for logit and fractional models
unresolved_confounders: The authors state the cross-sectional design and data do not facilitate causal inference regarding the effect of ownership on service quality
Selection of parents into providers with a specific ownership form, and of providers into geographical areas, is addressed only by observed local-government-level controls
Differential survey response by ownership (public and for-profit) is acknowledged but not corrected
Less readily observable dimensions of childcare quality are not measured

claims.statement: Compared with for-profit childcare centers, nonprofit centers score lower on Staff with other educational background/Enrolled children, conditional on 11 center- and local-government-level controls.

definition.value: A third dummy variable comparing nonprofit (=1) with for-profit (=0) ownership, included to facilitate testing of all three hypotheses. Ownership is taken from register data obtained from Statistics Denmark.

timing.value: Ownership form as registered in the 2018 Statistics Denmark population list of childcare centers, i.e. measured at the time of the survey (cross-section, 2018).

outcome.label: Staff with other educational background/Enrolled children

definition.value: Number of staff with other educational backgrounds (e.g., psychologists and physiotherapists), who are typically involved in caretaking on a case-by-case basis, divided by the number of enrolled children.

timing.value: The state of the center at the time of the 2018 survey, as reported by the center director. The study is a single 2018 cross-section, so the outcome is measured contemporaneously with the ownership form, not after it.

units.value: staff with other educational background per enrolled child

magnitude.interpretation: nonprofits have 0.006 (p < 0.01) fewer staff with other educational backgrounds per child compared to for-profit centers

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

timing.value: Ownership form as registered in the 2018 Statistics Denmark population list of childcare centers, i.e. measured at the time of the survey (cross-section, 2018).

outcome.label: Share of employees with min. 5 days of external professional development

definition.value: Share of center staff with completed external professional development of a minimum of 5 days within the last 12 months.

timing.value: Measured over the 12 months before the 2018 survey, as reported by the center director. The study is a single 2018 cross-section, so the outcome is measured contemporaneously with the ownership form, not after it.

estimand.target_population: Center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds in Denmark that are under the Danish law on childcare provision; the contrast is for-profit versus public providers.

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

timing.value: Measured over the week before the 2018 survey, as reported by the center director. The study is a single 2018 cross-section, so the outcome is measured contemporaneously with the ownership form, not after it.

estimand.target_population: Center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds in Denmark that are under the Danish law on childcare provision; the contrast is nonprofit versus public providers.
estimand.formal_query: E[Days with substitutes in the last week | ownership = nonprofit, X] - E[Days with substitutes in the last week | ownership = public, X], with X the 11 center- and local-government-level controls (no do-operator: the authors state the design does not support causal inference).

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

Multiple hypothesis testing across a large number of dependent variables and models

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark: official registration of childcare center ownership (no register code or variable name given)

definition.value: A third dummy variable comparing nonprofit (=1) with for-profit (=0) ownership, included to facilitate testing of all three hypotheses. Ownership is taken from register data obtained from Statistics Denmark.

timing.value: Ownership form as registered in the 2018 Statistics Denmark population list of childcare centers, i.e. measured at the time of the survey (cross-section, 2018).

definition.value: Index of the degree of parent involvement in social activities, built from four survey items and measured from 1 (low degree) to 5 (high degree).

timing.value: The state of the center at the time of the 2018 survey, as reported by the center director. The study is a single 2018 cross-section, so the outcome is measured contemporaneously with the ownership form, not after it.

magnitude.interpretation: nonprofit centers score 0.3 points (p < 0.05) lower compared to for-profit centers

estimand.target_population: Center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds in Denmark that are under the Danish law on childcare provision; the contrast is nonprofit versus for-profit providers.
estimand.formal_query: E[Parent involvement in activities | ownership = nonprofit, X] - E[Parent involvement in activities | ownership = for-profit, X], with X the 11 center- and local-government-level controls (no do-operator: the authors state the design does not support causal inference).

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

claims.statement: Compared with public childcare centers, for-profit centers score higher on Percent of center director's time with the children, conditional on 11 center- and local-government-level controls.

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark: official registration of childcare center ownership (no register code or variable name given)

definition.value: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the childcare center is registered as a for-profit provider and 0 if it is a public provider; public ownership is the reference category. Ownership is taken from register data obtained from Statistics Denmark, the national agency charged with the official registration of center ownership.

timing.value: Ownership form as registered in the 2018 Statistics Denmark population list of childcare centers, i.e. measured at the time of the survey (cross-section, 2018).

outcome.label: Percent of center director's time with the children

definition.value: The center director's own assessment of how much of a day the director spends with the children (in percent), used as a proxy for the leader's hands-on involvement in and monitoring of the center's caregiving practices.

timing.value: The center director's assessment of a typical day at the time of the 2018 survey. The study is a single 2018 cross-section, so the outcome is measured contemporaneously with the ownership form, not after it.

units.value: percentage points of the director's day

magnitude.interpretation: center directors of for-profit childcare centers report spending, on average, 17% (p < 0.001) more of their time with the children out of their day compared to public center directors

estimand.target_population: Center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds in Denmark that are under the Danish law on childcare provision; the contrast is for-profit versus public providers.
estimand.formal_query: E[Percent of center director's time with the children | ownership = for-profit, X] - E[Percent of center director's time with the children | ownership = public, X], with X the 11 center- and local-government-level controls (no do-operator: the authors state the design does not support causal inference).

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.

definition.value: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the childcare center is registered as a for-profit provider and 0 if it is a public provider; public ownership is the reference category. timing.value: Ownership form as registered in the 2018 Statistics Denmark population list of childcare centers, i.e. measured at the time of the survey (cross-section, 2018).

definition.value: Dummy for whether the center is fully or partially nature- or forest-based (yes = 1, no = 0).

timing.value: The state of the center at the time of the 2018 survey, as reported by the center director. The study is a single 2018 cross-section, so the outcome is measured contemporaneously with the ownership form, not after it.

units.value: probability (0-1) of being a completely or partially nature-based center

magnitude.interpretation: the probability of being a completely or partially nature-based center is 15 percentage points (p < 0.05) higher, when the center is for-profit compared to public

estimand.target_population: Center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds in Denmark that are under the Danish law on childcare provision; the contrast is for-profit versus public providers.
estimand.formal_query: E[Nature-based or combination | ownership = for-profit, X] - E[Nature-based or combination | ownership = public, X], with X the 11 center- and local-government-level controls (no do-operator: the authors state the design does not support causal inference).

population.description: Danish center-based childcare centers for 3-5-year-olds under the Danish law on childcare provision that responded to the author's 2018 nationwide survey of center directors; the final data comprise 249 public, 134 nonprofit and 208 for-profit centers.
population.ages: Centers caring for 3-5-year-old children (in age-integrated centers the director answered only for the 3-5-year-old kindergarten children)
population.period: 2018 (survey and administrative data; children of sole providers measured 2017)
population.selection: Disproportional stratified random sample from the Statistics Denmark population list of 3468 centers: all 501 for-profit and all 487 nonprofit centers plus 1000 randomly selected public centers; 1943 centers actually received the survey and 591 completed or partially completed it (response rate approx. 30%). Chi2 tests show the ownership distribution of respondents differs significantly from the sample for public and for-profit centers. Centers established under the law on public schools are excluded. Estimation samples are further reduced by item non-response.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used. Observed cross-sectional variation in registered provider ownership (public, nonprofit, for-profit) across Danish childcare centers in 2018, with regression adjustment for center- and local-government-level covariates. The author states that random assignment of centers to areas and children to centers was impossible, leaving a cross-sectional design that prevents causal inference.

key_assumptions.assumption: The cross-sectional design prevents causal inference: the reported difference is an association between provider ownership and the quality indicator, not an estimated effect of ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author states it twice, in the methods section and again among the limitations in the discussion.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning on the 11 center- and local-government-level covariates (child and family composition, capacity, opening hours, parents' financial situation, user fee, municipal demand, density, socio-economic index and sole-provider children) removes the confounding of the ownership-quality comparison. The author puts this only as making it more likely that remaining performance differences are attributable to ownership.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author motivates the controls by possible selection in the geographical location of providers and in parents' choice of provider ownership, and claims only that controlling 'increases the likelihood' that variation is attributable to ownership; no balance table or sensitivity analysis is offered.
